evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says: 'This should take about five to ten minutes of your time so we can build an accurate code. You can depend on. Would that be okay?' — framing present but time estimate is off (call runs 17 min, not 5-10), and rep does wait for yes.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Rep asks name (Kaylee Kennedy), moving day (week of 12th, Monday), route (4800 Cleveland Drive, Fort Worth to 8961 Risky Trail, same subdivision — two streets over), and size (1910 sq ft, 3 bedrooms, one story). All four covered.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks: 'What do you have any concerns or any important things that you wanted to answer during this call today?' Asked before any logistics probing. Customer raises: wants definite quote, flexible on dates (Mon-Thu week of 12th, knows cheaper Mon-Thu), no heavy items but has treadmill, about 50% house packed, needs packing help for garage/kitchen/large items, wants quote options (with packing help vs. self-packed), and is getting competitive quotes.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep says 'Uh-huh' and 'Okay' multiple times but does not dig deeper with 'tell me more' follow-ups. Customer's concern about packing cost structure ($200 supply fee vs. hourly) is acknowledged ('Okay, the packing cost would be $200') but not explored further. Customer's concern about treadmill disassembly ('it's not gonna fit through the door it has to be disassembled') is answered directly but not layered deeper. Rep does not systematically revisit or confirm all concerns were understood.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No reflection or summary of concerns. Rep never says 'So what I'm hearing is…' or confirms 'Did I get all of it?' Rep moves directly from customer concern-raising into logistics probing without a reflection checkpoint.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covers: property type (house), floor/stories (one story, confirmed), bedrooms (3), additional rooms (office, garage, laundry room, bathrooms), walking distance (1-20 feet from street to house if truck parked on street), access concerns (driveway can fit regular vehicle/box truck but not 18-wheeler). Second location mentioned but not fully probed (same subdivision, two streets over). All major items present.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Yes. Rep says: 'Since you have mentioned that we are packing partially, the packing cost would be $200 wherein we will bring my, the packing materials to pack.' Customer had already mentioned this need; rep confirms the service and cost.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes, though confusing. Rep initially says '$80, is this the total number of boxes?' then pivots to 'The estimated number of boxes based on your square footage would be about 95 to 115 boxes.' Customer pushes back on the inconsistency ('What, what was the first, what was the first number? Eighteen and how did we go to ninety to 150?'). Rep then clarifies customer filled out online as 80. The box count question was asked but the delivery was confused and contradictory.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full. Rep anchors to home size: 'A typical 1900 square foot home would normally take four movers and two trucks between five and a half to seven and a half hours.' Then personalizes to customer's situation: 'In your case we're coming from a one story house going to the new location which is like, two minutes away from the first location. So, we will split your moving to two days on the first day. We will partially pack all of the things. Then, we will be sending out two movers and one truck that is between seven to eight hours the following day. We will be sending out four movers and two trucks estimated time is between five and a half to seven and a half hours.' Final estimate: $4,662.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Rep discloses: $97/hour per mover, $200 supply fee (packing materials), 2.5-hour minimum, prorated into 15-minute increments, no hidden fees (credit card, sterile, disassemble/reassembly). Rep frames: 'everything is included on the $97 per hour per mover' except packing supplies. Transparency is clear.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After quote of $4,662, customer responds 'Wow. Okay, a lot more than I thought it would be. Okay, alright, alright! You can send me the quote the estimate.' Rep does not ask 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent; no pause held for a genuine silence response.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Partial. Rep mentions 'we also remove feature and on time guarantee' but does not explain the discount terms (starts discounting immediately if late). The statement is vague and incomplete.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full. Rep says: 'First is that we have no worry damage coverage included on the RU rate that you're paying us. We will provide up to $2,000 per move. That is to repair, replace and reimburse for items.' Covers $2,000 limit, built into the rate (not an add-on). No deductible or fine-print language explicitly mentioned, but framing is clear it's included.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. After Two Promises, rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar. Rep pivots directly to final close/send quote without confirming customer's concerns about the two promises have been addressed.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep goes directly to sending the quote and saying 'feel free to shop around.' No genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or equivalent question is asked.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False. No 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' type question is asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or a direct close. Rep says 'I'll send you the code so you can be able to review it and feel free to shop around if you find a better rate.' This is the opposite of an explicit ask — it explicitly gives the customer an out.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False. No mention of rate lock, booking guarantee, or deposit terms.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None. No date, time window, crew size, or addresses confirmed for booking. Rep offers to send the estimate and encourages shopping around; call ends without a booking or next steps confirmed.

top_strength: Rep expertly gathered all logistics details (square footage, bedrooms, rooms, access, walking distance) and delivered a fully anchored, personalized estimate ($4,662 split over two days with specific crew counts and times) tailored to the customer's short-distance move and packing needs.
coaching_note: After quoting, rep must ask 'Does that feel fair?' and hold silence for a genuine response before pivoting to close; rep also skipped the final concerns check entirely and never asked for the business — these are the two highest-leverage gaps between the estimate and a confirmed booking.
